<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The reconciliation notebook is extensive.

The notebook will be designed for Charles to run. It saves progress after each county and resumes from where it left off. Existing parsers will be reused.

The handoff covers six jobs: inventory source families, reconcile people conservatively, check cross-county routes from both ends, verify program identities and totals, produce actionable summaries, and save and resume.

A single failed county must not halt the entire run. Missing school applicant pages should not fail other checks. Counties will not be declared scientifically ready. Name-free aggregates will be stored in the repository.

Private ledgers will remain on the Desktop. The notebook will export only counts and plain-language findings, never names.

Resume logic will fingerprint source files and skip counties whose verified work is unchanged.

Charles will handle the expensive processing. Progress will be printed conversationally.

Only eleven of seventy-five counties have complete school applicant pages.

The eleven counties with applicant pages are AB, CS, GL, TL, AR, SB, B, CT, PH, TM, and CJ.

For counties without applicant pages, the notebook will skip person reconciliation between School Applicant View and School Result View. It will still inventory families and compare school results internally.

Resident lists will be compared to school results where resident pages exist, flagged as incomplete when absent. Incoming candidates will be checked against incoming admitted and rejected totals. Outgoing destinations will be aggregated and matched against incoming admitted counts at those destinations. Program occupancy will be verified against placement row counts.

Cross-county individual matching will follow a two-step approach: first compare aggregate origin and destination counts, then report whether individual matches are uniquely supported. Full individual matching between outgoing and incoming records requires name and score keys and is treated as provisional.

Matching will run entirely in memory. Only aggregate counts will be exported: uniquely matched, ambiguous, and unmatched. No names will enter the repository.

The resume fingerprint will hash each county’s status.json slice, including saved pages, unresolved URLs, discovered lengths, and page file mtimes. Each county will be processed independently and flushed to disk.

The resume fingerprint will hash each county’s checkpoint files by path, size, and mtime, plus the manifest stat. This catches replaced pages that retain the same count. The notebook will be a single module with a directory scanner and a per-county SHA256 fingerprinter.

The notebook will be organized into focused functions. `inventory_county` will catalog families without requiring completeness. `load_verified_family_rows` will load pages or flag missing records without aborting the county run. Separate functions will handle school result structure, resident versus results, incoming internal checks, and program totals. The applicant versus results check will be skipped with an explanatory note when no applicant pages exist. Each function will catch its own errors so one county failure does not halt the entire batch.

Cross-county and individual matching are deferred passes. They require all counties to first save their outgoing and incoming aggregate counters.

Each county will write its results to a timestamped subdirectory under outputs/romania_2001_all_county_offline_reconciliation/. That folder will hold the county inventory, findings, summaries, fingerprints, and cross-county flows.

Cross-county flows may be built incrementally from per-county outgoing and incoming counters.

Each county will write its outgoing and incoming-admitted counters as name-free JSON. A final cell will combine all counties into cross-county flows.

Resume logic will skip a county if its fingerprint matches the saved fingerprint and the county JSON exists.

The notebook will have six cells: a markdown overview, settings for counties, checks, resume flag, and private root, module loading, the county loop, a cross-county combination cell, a summary table, and a results guide.

A quick syntax and import check will run first. A dry inventory of one small county may follow, but only if it is inexpensive; Alba would be too slow because of full page hash verification. The cost of verified_page and the original family manifest structure need review. Snapshot and live inventories will be compared to surface discrepancies.

The live inventory is current through 2026-10-14 11:08:40, which exceeds the snapshot date. A field-by-field comparison will exclude the refreshed timestamp.

Charles has waived notebook formatting rules. The new notebook will be created directly with Write rather than through EditNotebook.

The new notebook will use the sports_net kernel metadata from an existing county progress notebook. For counties with no applicant pages, all_gymnasium_rows will be skipped entirely. For the eleven counties with complete pages, that function will be called inside a try/except block so any directory or page errors are caught and recorded without halting the run.

A quick Python check will identify any counties with partial applicant pages. Program identity checks will catch source_programs disagreements and record them in plain language instead of aborting. The program check will read each county's manifest directly to avoid importing the full program identity gate.

Program checks will sum occupancy of admitted versus saved placement rows. If placement views are reconciled, the code will compare combined verified program row counts to that occupancy and record any mismatch in plain language. HERO or success labels will not be computed.

School result versus applicant matching will only run when both the school directory is complete and every applicant page exists for a county. It will use all_gymnasium_rows and compare name-score multisets by school code.

School result versus applicant matching will report same-school matches, unmatched applicant rows, unmatched result rows, and repeated keys. Result-only rows will not be added to the score population.

Cross-county outgoing placed counts will be drawn from school results whose Liceu suffix names another county. Incoming counts will be drawn from incoming_admitted, incoming_rejected, and incoming_candidates by origin suffix. Each pair will be compared by outgoing count versus destination incoming admitted count. Individual matching will compare name-score multisets between outgoing rows and incoming admitted rows.

Individual matching will be memory-efficient. Roughly 200,000 admission rows across 41 counties are manageable.

Only aggregate counts will be exported. These include pairs that agree in total, pairs that disagree, and within agreeing pairs the number of unique matches versus ambiguous ones.

Rows without a readable county suffix will be counted but not guessed.

For counties with unresolved school result URLs such as BN and SV, person checks will mark the check as partial rather than fail the entire county.

Saved pages will be compared directly. Any remaining unresolved school-result URL will be flagged as one unresolved address. Missing resident records will be reported as absent from the saved subset rather than from the county itself. The exact return behavior of checked_page and verified_page still needs verification.

- **Resident applicant list.** An incomplete list is a saved subset. People on missing pages are not dropped from the county and are not counted as unsuccessful.
- **Incoming row comparisons.** Printed name and admission score, with repeats kept. An incoming applicant row without an outcome row is unresolved.

cells.append(new_code_cell("""# CELL 4 — Outgoing placements versus incoming admissions. No archive requests.
if "run_folder" not in dir():
    run_folder = recon.latest_run(OUTPUT_ROOT)
flow_counts = recon.cross_county_routes(run_folder)
print("Pair rows:", len(flow_counts))
print("Saved table:", run_folder / "cross_county_flow_counts.csv")
if len(flow_counts):
    disagree = flow_counts.loc[~flow_counts["aggregate_counts_agree"]]
    print("Pairs whose aggregate counts differ:", len(disagree))
    display_columns = [
        "origin_county", "destination_county",
        "school_result_outgoing_rows", "incoming_admitted_rows",
        "aggregate_counts_agree", "unique_name_score_keys_on_both_sides",
        "keys_only_on_school_result", "keys_only_on_incoming_admitted",
        "ambiguous_keys", "comparison_scope",
    ]
    display(flow_counts[display_columns].head(30))
"""))

cells.append(new_markdown_cell("""## Cell 5 — Read the county summaries

The table is name-free. `plain_summary` is the sentence to read first. `next_source_question` is the specific gap, when one remains. A county with every known URL address saved can still be missing the School Applicant View, which is a different webpage family.
"""))

cells.append(new_code_cell("""# CELL 5 — Show the saved county summaries.
if "run_folder" not in dir():
    run_folder = recon.latest_run(OUTPUT_ROOT)
summary = recon.summary_frame(run_folder)
columns = [
    "county", "county_name",
    "school_applicant_pages_saved", "school_applicant_pages_expected",
    "school_result_pages_verified", "school_result_pages_expected",
    "school_result_unresolved_urls",
    "resident_pages_saved", "resident_pages_projected",
    "outgoing_rows_with_other_county_suffix",
    "original_placement_shortfall", "remaining_placement_shortfall",
    "next_source_question",
]
print(f"{len(summary)} counties in {run_folder.name}")
summary[columns]
"""))

cells.append(new_markdown_cell("""## What a count does and does not establish

- **School Applicant View saved / listed schools.** File coverage against the origin school directory. Person comparison with the School Result View runs only when every listed school page is present. A missing page stays unresolved.
- **School Result View verified / target.** Hash-checked pages, including the finding that a target can be a projection. Unresolved URL addresses stay open. BN and SV each had one unresolved School Result View URL address in the October 14 inventory. This notebook does not close them.
- **Resident applicant list.** An incomplete list is a saved subset. People on missing pages are not dropped from the county and are not counted as unsuccessful.
- **Incoming row comparisons.** Printed name and admission score, with repeats kept. An incoming applicant row without an outcome row is unresolved.
- **Outgoing suffix.** A School Result View destination label that ends in another county code. It is an observed admissions route.
- **Placement shortfall.** Occupancy admitted total minus the original county admitted list. Program-specific recovery can reduce the **remaining** shortfall without forcing the original gap to zero.
- **Unique name-and-score key.** One printed name and admission score occurring once on each side of a county pair. Aggregate agreement does not by itself establish that link. The masked personal identifier means even a unique key is provisional.
- **Next source question.** The concrete missing evidence. It is not a label that the county is ready for a national outcome model.

Full sentences for every finished county are in `report.md` inside the run folder. Pair counts are in `cross_county_flow_counts.csv`.
"""))

})
nbformat.write(nb, path)
print(path)
print("cells", len(nb.cells))
PY

    assert 12.0 <= client.interval < start

    assert 0 < cut <= 0.10

    # failure uses 1.75, not the 10% bump: reconstruct from saved interval

    before = 20.0

    print("failure factor", FAILURE_SLOWDOWN_FACTOR, "interval", client.interval)

The scientific stack is current. The last install was 15 July 2026, about three months ago, and it is already on the present major lines: Python 3.11.11, NumPy 2.4.6, pandas 3.0.3, SciPy 1.17.1, Matplotlib 3.11.0, and scikit-learn 1.8.0. JupyterLab 4.5.7 and the notebook kernel are in place. I would leave this environment alone while the Romania pages are still downloading.

Python 3.11 is the right line to finish on. It keeps receiving security fixes through October 2027, and moving to 3.12 or 3.13 would risk the notebooks for no gain in the analysis. pandas 3 is the one behavior change already in effect: Copy-on-Write is always on. The notebooks have been running on that since July.

The part I would not treat as healthy is how the packages were mixed. About 133 packages come from Anaconda defaults and 61 from conda-forge. The July install pulled NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and Matplotlib from conda-forge and left NumPy linked to the Netlib reference BLAS, the slow generic linear-algebra library, in place of OpenBLAS. That is fine for the page checks. It is a poor base for the network and scoring work. The next `conda update --all` on this same environment is the likely way to break Matplotlib or the linear-algebra libraries.

When you do want a refresh, make a new environment from conda-forge only, with OpenBLAS, and keep `sports_net` as the one the notebooks already run.
